name: Roastbook
use_label: Log espresso shots on your own server
one_liner: A self-hosted coffee journal that reads a photographed bag’s label and fills in the details for you.

text.why: Keeping a record of beans, roasters and brews usually means the data lives on someone else’s server. Roastbook is meant to run on your own, and a single photo of the bag fills in origin, variety and roast level; typing a roaster’s name looks up its site and location. A quick brew log takes three numbers.
text.take: Having a read-only demo on bundled sample data means you can see the real screens before installing anything.
build: It runs on PostgreSQL and your own storage, deployed with one Docker Compose command or a Helm chart. The AI features that read a label or research a roaster turn on once OPENAI_API_KEY is set; everything else works without a key. The repository states there are no accounts, no telemetry and no upsell.

who.role: Home espresso and brew enthusiasts, and anyone who wants their coffee log kept on their own server.

start.text: Try the read-only demo at roastbook.vercel.app first, then deploy it yourself with Docker Compose.

caveat: The AI features need your own OpenAI key and cost accordingly. It is early — two stars.

license.scope_text: Use, change and redistribute, commercially too. Keep the notice.

numbers.star_delta_unit: GitHub stars gained in the window, GH Archive events summed to as_of
numbers.method: Star total = the value last checked on GitHub (stars_checked_at) + increases observed via GH Archive since. The 24h · 7d · 30d gains are GH Archive hourly events summed to the reference time (as_of). No score of ours.
